subject: Agriculture
title: Phylloxera and Wine
description: A 60-second lesson on Phylloxera and Wine.

hook.text: In the 1860s, a tiny insect from America nearly destroyed every vineyard in Europe. Wine itself almost died.

buildup.text: Phylloxera—a root-feeding aphid—hitchhiked on American vine imports. European vines had no resistance.

discovery.text: Within 30 years, phylloxera destroyed 70% of France's vineyards. The wine industry faced total collapse.

twist.text: The solution: graft European vines onto resistant American rootstock. Nearly all wine today still grows this way.

climax.text: Phylloxera taught agriculture that genetic diversity is insurance. Monocultures invite catastrophe.

punchline.text: French wine survives on American roots. The pest created a permanent marriage.

quiz.question: How was the phylloxera crisis in European vineyards solved?
options: Grafting European vines onto resistant American rootstock
